text:
maria: Canary rollout for inference-gateway stalled in eu-west1, looks like the post-upgrade init never finished. Helm says RELEASED but traffic not flipping. Anyone digging? :thinking_face:

josh: I see pods stuck in `Init:0/1` on the canary. `kubectl describe` shows the init container waiting on CRD conversion webhook. Getting repeated 429s from the webhook.

sanjay: Confirmed. API server logs show `conversion webhook returned 429` for the gpupool.crd group. Could be rate limiting on the conversion service (it's a small lambda behind nginx).

maria: Oh — that conversion service was recently rolled in the infra pipeline, right? Might be a capacity/regional constraint. eu-west got lower concurrency on that Lambda after the tf change.

josh: Also noticed nodepool autoscaler didn't create extra nodes for the canary. Terraform repo recently applied a change that reduced `max_nodes` for the gpu pool in eu-west1 to save cost. That could explain ImagePull/Pending if we're oversubscribed.

laura: I'm on the infra TF run that made the max_nodes change. We reduced max from 6 -> 3 in eu-west to cut costs after low usage. We didn't realize canary spikes would need the extra node. Sorry.

maria: Ok two separate issues then: 1) conversion webhook returning 429 -> init stuck, 2) infra scaling constraint -> scheduling pressure. Both can block the Helm canary hook job and leave the release effectively stuck.

josh: Workaround idea: roll back the webhook deployment to the previous replica count (increase concurrency), and temporarily bump gpu nodepool max to 6, then re-run the helm canary. Quick commands:
```bash
# infra (apply quick override)
cd infra/eu-west1/gpu-pool
terraform apply -var='gpu_max=6' -auto-approve

# rollout webhook back up
kubectl scale deploy gpupool-conversion -n infra --replicas=3
```

sanjay: I can scale the conversion service now. Laura, can you submit a quick TF change to bump `gpu_max`? If not I can run an emergency apply with owner's ok.

laura: Giving you verbal OK, sanjay. I pushed a tiny TF bump to the emergency branch and triggered the pipeline. CI shows `apply` in progress.

maria: While that's running, I'm going to attempt `helm rollback` for the canary release to stop traffic and avoid client impact. Plan: rollback 1 revision but keep the CRs so we don't lose state.

josh: Heads-up: Helm rollback will not fix init containers blocked by webhook. But it will free up canary replicas so the autoscaler isn't further stressed.

deploy-bot: rollout/helm-release inference-gateway-canary rollback started by maria at 2009876610

sanjay: Conversion service scaled to 3 replicas. Monitoring logs — 5xx/429s dropping.

laura: Terraform apply finished: gpu_max set to 6. Nodes provisioning now (GKE autoscaler events incoming).

maria: Helm rollback completed, release back to previous revision. Canary pods terminating.

josh: New nodes joined the cluster, pending pods are now scheduling. I'm re-triggering the helm canary upgrade on a fresh pipeline run (no CR changes).

sanjay: Re-run showed the init container now passes — webhook conversion responding 200s. Canary hook job completed successfully.

maria: Canary progressed to 30% then 100%, no errors. Closing the thread.

laura: Follow-ups: I'll open a PR to add a Terraform guardrail so we don't drop gpu_max below a threshold when canaries are scheduled, and add a circuit-breaker on the conversion webhook to avoid 429s under transient cold starts.

maria: Thanks all :pray: Good catch and quick remediation.
